note: The two sets are essentially identical in content: both capture the s-coordinate endpoints, the flatback trailing-edge definition, the ontology definition, and the modal damping values, and both make the same two errors (edgewise damping given as 5% where the page says 3%, and a garbled 'flatback surface | midpoint definition | normalized arc length position' claim whose quote is cut off and whose value is misbound). The only difference is that set A keeps 'following the curved blade reference axis' as an explicit condition on the composite-layers definition while set B folds it into the value; both are faithful. Neither set captures the stiffness-matrix/tool-chain facts (PreComp, VABS, BECAS, OpenFAST, HAWC2).
remarks: Both sets misread the damping sentence: the page states 3%, 3%, and 6% for flapwise, edgewise and torsional modes, but both quote and extract 5% for the edgewise mode. Both repeat the s=0 and s=1 endpoint facts twice under two entity names ('normalized arc length position coordinate (s)' and 'normalized arc length position'). Both include the figure-2-7 annotation labels (Plane of Rotation, Chord Line, Arc Width, Offset, Pitch Axis, θrot) as bare 'has component/has property' claims with no engineering content. Both omit the important facts that stiffness matrices per cross section were computed with PreComp/VABS (NREL) or BECAS (DTU) and used in OpenFAST or HAWC2. The text layer garbles 'zero' as 'ero' in one quote and the last claim's quote is cut off ('For ﬂat ge is deﬁned...'), which both sets reproduced.
